claims.text: A tungsten-based refractory high-entropy alloy containing controlled coherent nanoprecipitates will resist erosion by high-temperature liquid aluminum significantly better than conventional hot-dip-plating materials.
The proposed material is a tungsten-based refractory high-entropy alloy engineered to contain coherent nanoprecipitates.
The tungsten-based refractory HEA can be used to fabricate rollers, guide plates, and other critical dipping and plating equipment parts.
Coherent nanoprecipitates stabilize the microstructure of the tungsten-rich matrix.
Coherent nanoprecipitates promote formation of a protective, adherent oxide scale on the alloy surface.
Coherent nanoprecipitate interfaces facilitate dislocation transmission and relieve stress concentrations that could cause premature cracking.
The tungsten-based refractory HEA has high elevated-temperature strength.
The tungsten-based refractory HEA has intrinsic corrosion resistance.
The engineered nanoprecipitates aid formation of a stable protective oxide layer.
A stable protective oxide layer reduces direct chemical attack by molten aluminum.
Some refractory high-entropy alloys can form a protective oxide layer during high-temperature oxidation.
Parts made from the proposed HEA will have lower erosion or material-loss rates under molten-aluminum exposure than conventional-alloy parts.
Parts made from the proposed HEA will retain superior mechanical integrity under hot-dip aluminum processing conditions.
Parts made from the proposed HEA will have a longer service life than conventional-alloy parts.
Conventional alloys used for these parts undergo significant erosion and require frequent maintenance or replacement during prolonged molten-aluminum contact.
The proposed protective effect is expected under typical hot-dip aluminum plating temperatures and chemical conditions.
Extreme thermal cycling or unexpected impurities may alter the proposed material's performance.
The quantitative improvement in erosion resistance and the long-term stability of the oxide scale in a real plating environment have not been established.
